node-1.label: Dyspnea on exertion and syncope during exercise

node-2.label: Patient in their 80s with medical history of essential hypertension and Parkinson disease

node-3.label: Patient reported dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance for the past year, with difficulty walking more than 100m, and experienced syncope during a bicycle ride with loss of consciousness for a few minutes followed by complete recovery

node-4.label: Physical examination showed elevated blood pressure of 150/78 mm Hg with normal breath and heart sounds and no murmurs

why.why: Echocardiography excludes significant structural or valvular disease, and physical examination showed normal heart sounds with no murmurs. Although exertional syncope initially raised the possibility of outflow obstruction, the absence of valvular/structural abnormalities makes this very unlikely. Confidence is lowered from 0.2 to 0.05.

Expert analyses by the laboratory physician and radiologist independently confirm that the resting ECG and Holter findings—first-degree AV block with bifascicular block, intermittent third-degree AV block, and bradycardia (36 bpm)—directly explain the exertional dyspnea and exercise-induced syncope. The newly noted normal thyroid function further excludes reversible metabolic causes, while normal troponin, electrolytes, and echocardiography exclude ischemia and structural/valvular disease. Confidence is raised from 0.9 to 0.95.

Expert analyses reaffirm that normal troponin, electrolytes, and echocardiography exclude acute ischemia and structural disease. The confirmed intermittent third-degree AV block with bifascicular block fully accounts for the clinical picture, making ischemic heart disease very unlikely. Confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.10.

Syncope occurred during exercise rather than in a typical autonomic precipitating setting, and the confirmed severe conduction disorder fully accounts for the symptoms. Parkinson disease alone is insufficient to support autonomic dysfunction as the cause. Confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.05.

node-11.label: Laboratory tests show normal troponin and normal electrolytes

node-12.label: Echocardiography excludes significant structural or valvular disease

node-13.label: Patient has intermittent third-degree AV block with bifascicular block as the underlying conduction disorder

The additional normal thyroid function result rules out metabolic mimics, and normal troponin, electrolytes, and echocardiography exclude ischemic, structural, and valvular alternatives. Confidence is raised from 0.9 to 0.95.
